QuickCapture.Guide.Title: Start taking notes
QuickCapture.Guide.Body:
# Start with one note

This sample note is yours to edit or delete. Enter text, then switch between **Edit** and **Preview** to see your Markdown.

## What you can do

- Capture ideas, meeting notes, links, and temporary information; a title is optional
- Pin frequently used content to the Pinned tab and unpin it whenever you need to
- With clipboard history enabled, copied text, links, and images appear in the Clipboard tab
- Drag images or files into a note, or add and remove attachments in its details
- Search titles and note text to find an earlier record

## Markdown cheat sheet

| What to write | Example input |
| --- | --- |
| Bold text | `**Important**` |
| Task list | `- [ ] Follow up` |
| Link | `[DeskBox](https://deskbox.fun)` |

```md
## Meeting notes
- [ ] Confirm the next step
- [ ] Attach the reference material
```

> This sample is ordinary content. Once you rewrite it, it stays with your notes.

Todo.Guide.Notes:
# Use this task to explore Todo

Check the three steps above one by one. When they are all complete, the task moves to Completed; you can uncheck it to keep working.

## Task details

| Feature | When it helps |
| --- | --- |
| Importance and color | Separate priorities, projects, or contexts |
| Date and reminder | Set a follow-up time for time-sensitive work |
| Recurrence | Handle daily, weekly, or regular tasks |
| Attachments | Keep reference files, images, or materials |

## Write the details in Notes

Put longer context, decisions, and progress here with Markdown. You can also add lists and code-style text:

```text
Meeting outcome
1. Confirm the owner
2. Follow up on Friday
```

- [ ] Add background information
- [ ] Attach reference material

> Delete or rewrite this sample task, then start adding your own.

Settings.Dialog.AboutMeP1: I like the native feel of Microsoft apps, and I like widgets that keep useful information and tools close on the desktop.

Onboarding.Intro.Title: DeskBox
Onboarding.Intro.Body: Keep files, notes, and tasks together in lightweight desktop widgets
Onboarding.Step1.Title: A lightweight organizing layer on your desktop
Onboarding.Step1.Body: DeskBox doesn't replace your Windows desktop. It puts files, search, and everyday tools into lightweight widgets — visible when you need them, quiet when you don't.
Onboarding.Step1.Hint1: Doesn't replace Windows desktop — every action is reversible
Onboarding.Step1.Hint2: Widgets can be freely moved and resized

Onboarding.Step2.Hint2: Path and pin status can be changed anytime in Settings

Onboarding.Step3.Hint1: The accent color affects highlight elements in widgets

Onboarding.Task.Step1.Title: Your first file widget is on the right
Onboarding.Task.Step1.Body: A file widget is a place to organize files on your desktop. Put frequently used files in it, then show or hide it anytime.
Onboarding.Task.Step1.LocationBody: The widget starts on the right side of the current display. You can move and resize it.
Onboarding.Task.Step1.LocalBody: DeskBox uses local folders directly and does not upload files on its own.
Onboarding.Task.Step1.ToggleBody: Hide the widget when you do not need it, then show it again with the shortcut or tray icon.
Onboarding.Task.Step2.Title: Choose where collected files are stored
Onboarding.Task.Step2.Body: A collection widget is not a shortcut. Files you drag or paste are moved or copied into the storage path below. Every collection widget creates its own folder under this path.
Onboarding.Task.Step2.ManagedBody: Files in every collection widget are physically stored in their own folder under the path above.
Onboarding.Task.Step2.MappedBody: Show an existing folder as a widget. Files stay in their original location, and widget actions affect them directly.
Onboarding.Task.Step2.TransferTitle: What happens when you add files
Onboarding.Task.Step2.TransferSummary: Current setting: {0} files into the matching widget folder under this path.
Onboarding.Task.Step2.StatusReady: Select “Show widget” to display it on the right.
Onboarding.Task.Step2.StatusShown: The file widget is visible on the right.
Onboarding.Task.Step2.StatusUnavailable: No file widget was found. You can create one later by right-clicking the tray icon.
Onboarding.Task.Step3.Title: Put files in a widget
Onboarding.Task.Step3.Body: Drag a file from the desktop or File Explorer. DeskBox moves it into this widget's folder.
Onboarding.Task.Step3.DragBody: Drag a file from the desktop or File Explorer into the widget.
Onboarding.Task.Step3.PasteBody: Copy a file, select the widget, then press Ctrl+V.
Onboarding.Task.Step3.AddBody: Select “Add file” in the widget, then choose a file.
Onboarding.Task.Step3.StatusReady: Try dragging one file into the widget.
Onboarding.Task.Step3.StatusShown: Try dragging one file into the widget.
Onboarding.Task.Step3.SkipTip: You can continue without adding a file.
Onboarding.Task.Step4.Title: Show them anytime. Hide them when done.
Onboarding.Task.Step4.Body: Bring your widgets in front of any window and use their content without leaving what you are doing.
Onboarding.Task.Step4.ToggleBody: Press {0}, or select the DeskBox icon at the right of the taskbar. Repeat to hide them.
Onboarding.Task.Step4.TrayBody: Right-click the DeskBox icon at the right of the taskbar to create a widget, map another folder as a widget, or open Settings.
Onboarding.Task.Step4.MappedEntry: Map a folder as a widget
Onboarding.Task.Step4.FeatureEntry: Feature widget: add To Do, Notes, Weather, or Music
Onboarding.Task.Step4.StatusReady: Try hiding the widgets, then show them again.
Onboarding.Task.Step4.StatusToggled: The widgets were toggled. Select again to restore the previous state.
Onboarding.Task.Step4.StatusHidden: Widgets are hidden. Select again to show them.
Onboarding.Task.Step4.StatusShown: Widgets are visible. Select again to hide them.
Onboarding.Task.Step5.Title: Add the features you need
Onboarding.Task.Step5.Body: These features are optional. Turn one on to add its widget to the desktop.
Onboarding.Task.Step5.Done1: Know where the first file widget is
Onboarding.Task.Step5.Done3: Show or hide widgets with the shortcut or tray icon
Onboarding.Task.Step5.Done4: Create widgets from the tray menu
Onboarding.Task.Step5.OptionalBody: You can change these anytime in Settings > Feature widgets.
Widget.Empty.ActionsHint: Drag files or press Ctrl+V to paste

Onboarding.Task.Step2.Warning.CloudSync: DeskBox does not upload files itself. If this is a OneDrive or other synced folder, that service may sync the files.
Onboarding.Task.Step2.Warning.Removable: Files in collection widgets will be unavailable while this drive is disconnected.
Onboarding.Task.Step2.Warning.Network: Files in collection widgets will be unavailable while this network location is disconnected.
Onboarding.Task.Step3.StatusCompleted: The file was moved into the widget.
